hook.text: In 2001, coffee prices crashed to a 100-year low. Farmers across Latin America and Africa were devastated.

buildup.text: Overproduction—especially from Vietnam's rapid expansion—flooded the market with cheap Robusta, collapsing prices.

discovery.text: Prices fell below production cost. Farmers abandoned farms, children left school, and entire communities collapsed.

twist.text: The International Coffee Agreement, which had stabilized prices with export quotas, had been dissolved in 1989.

climax.text: Without a price floor, free market forces destroyed livelihoods. The crisis reshaped how the industry thinks about sustainability.

punchline.text: The market crashed, millions suffered, and nothing protected them.
